newsitem.title: MONACO: OLYMPICS-IOC SAYS IT HAS NO EVIDENCE OF CORRUPTION.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-IOC SAYS IT HAS NO EVIDENCE OF CORRUPTION.

text.p: Olympic chiefs said on Tuesday that they had found no evidence to support allegations of corruption in the boxing events at the 1988 Seoul Games after studying accusations that judges were bribed to back South Koreans.
The International Olympic Committee (IOC) said it had found no proof to support accusations that American light-middleweight Roy Jones was cheated out of a gold medal by bribed judges.
"There is no evidence of corruption in the boxing events in Seoul," IOC director general Francois Carrard said after the IOC announced it would not be taking any action in the case.
Jones, who went on to become a professional world champion, was beaten in the 1988 final by South Korean Park Si-hun in an extraordinary judging decision.
Most spectators and commentators present had Jones way ahead of his outclassed opponent but three judges from Morocco, Uruguay and Uganda gave the decision to Park.

Last year the IOC appointed a commission to investigate the allegations that some judges were bribed in favour of South Koreans and that some international boxing officials were aware of the cheating.
But the IOC said in a statement: "The facts obtained by the working group have not added any new elements that would warrant reviewing the decision taken by the judges."
Carrard said he had travelled to Morocco in March to discuss the affair with the Moroccan judge in the Jones fight, Hiouad Larbi, who denies taking bribes. The IOC also studied videos of the bout.

"Larbi made an excellent impression," Carrard said. "He said that if he had to judge it today he would judge it in exactly the same way, although he acknowledged that some people might see it another way."
